courses.name: How machines work
courses.why: Every tool, bike and appliance is built from six simple parts; seeing them lets a person fix, buy and choose better.

courses.name: The engine in your life
courses.why: Car, mower and generator engines cost real money; knowing how they run helps with buying and repair choices.
units: Cars today versus a century ago

courses.name: Electricity at home, safely
courses.why: Electricity is in every home and a few ideas keep people safe and save money.
units: A circuit you can build safely

courses.name: Physics you can see in everyday motion
courses.why: Brakes, ramps, swings and sports all follow a few rules about force and motion.

sources.title: Fundamentals of Physics I (PHYS 200)
sources.licenceSeen: Open Yale Courses Terms of Use page and the course page: 'licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-Noncommercial-Share Alike 3.0 license'
sources.terms: Non-commercial only (Terms section 5). Third-party content is not covered unless a lecture's Credits section says so. Terms say nothing about AI or ingestion; check Yale's Office of General Counsel before any commercial use.
coursework: 24 video lectures (mp4, ogv, mov on the Archive)
sources.needIt: Explains why things move the way they do, the base for every machine, car and tool.
sources.notes: The Archive item says 'Yale University 2010. Some rights reserved', CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 US, with third-party credits excepted. Page for the course lists lectures 1 to 18 and 20 to 24 (lecture 19 not listed). It says solutions are posted but does not link the problem sets, so confirm what is downloadable. Calculus-based; rebuild at plain level. A second Archive item, oyc_Fundamentals_of_Physics_I, has audio only (24 mp3). Audit 16 Nov 2026: the course page lists 23 lectures (no 19); the Archive has 24 videos.

sources.title: MIT 8.01 Physics I: Classical Mechanics (Fall 1999)
sources.licenceSeen: Archive item page: 'Creative Commons Attribution-Noncommercial-Share Alike 3.0 United States'.
sources.terms: Non-commercial and share-alike under CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 US; nothing about AI on the Archive page. The current OCW Terms page allows AI use with attribution for non-commercial use.
sources.needIt: Famous demonstration lectures on force, motion, springs and fluids that make physics visible.
sources.notes: 35 lectures plus an introduction and a bonus video. The OCW 1999 page was not opened; archive metadata shows 71 mp4 files (two renditions), licence also in item metadata. Terms of OCW (non-commercial, attribution) apply. Pair with the 8.01SC coursework.

sources.title: Classical Mechanics (8.01SC, Fall 2016)
sources.by: Prof. Deepto Chakrabarty, Dr. Peter Dourmashkin and others, MIT
sources.licenceSeen: OCW course page footer links the Creative Commons licence; OCW Terms page states CC BY-NC-SA 4.0
sources.terms: OCW Terms page: content may be used to train and improve AI models with attribution, non-commercial use only, and derived models must carry CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 or a compatible licence.
sources.needIt: Self-paced physics with problem sets so a learner can check their own understanding.
sources.notes: OCW lists Lecture Videos and Problem Sets; videos are on OCW and are not downloaded here. Undergraduate; rebuild at plain level.

sources.title: How and Why Machines Work (2.000, Spring 2002)
sources.by: Prof. Joseph Smith and Prof. Martin Culpepper, MIT
sources.licenceSeen: OCW course page footer links the Creative Commons licence; OCW Terms page states CC BY-NC-SA 4.0
sources.terms: OCW Terms page: content may be used to train and improve AI models with attribution, non-commercial use only, and derived models must carry CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 or a compatible licence.
sources.needIt: Takes machines apart in the mind and in the hand: sketches, mechanisms, why each part is shaped as it is.
sources.notes: Undergraduate, hands-on. OCW lists Lecture Notes and Written Assignments, no videos or exams. The exact fit for a plain-language machines course.

sources.title: Basic machines and how they work
sources.by: US Bureau of Naval Personnel (Dover reprint of the 1965 edition)
sources.licence: US government work (not stated on page)
sources.licenceSeen: Archive page shows no copyright or licence statement, only a Terms of Service link. Author on the page is the US Bureau of Naval Personnel; US federal authorship is the basis.
sources.needIt: Teaches levers, pulleys, gears, screws and wheels with simple pictures, the parts inside every machine.
sources.notes: The Dover reprint adds a publisher; Dover's own cover or layout may be separately claimed. Prefer the original Navy text. Related Archive items: micro_IA41153602_0959 (1965 Navy course, ERIC), navedtra-14037-basic-machines-1994 (a 1994 NAVEDTRA with no licence text on its page). Audit 16 Nov 2026: this item is the 1971 Dover reprint; its licence is inferred from the Navy original. Prefer an original Navy scan when building.

sources.title: How it Works
sources.licenceSeen: Project Gutenberg ebook page, Copyright line reads 'Public domain in the USA.'
sources.needIt: A friendly early 1900s tour of how bridges, engines, clocks and telephones work.
sources.notes: Out of date on technology (telegraph, early autos, steam). Facts must be checked.

sources.title: Gas and Oil Engines, Simply Explained
sources.licenceSeen: Project Gutenberg ebook page, Copyright line reads 'Public domain in the USA.'
sources.needIt: Explains the four-stroke engine and carburetor in everyday words, useful for anyone with a car, mower or generator.
sources.notes: Published 1905 per the Gutenberg page. Early engine designs and fuels (including leaded gasoline). Flag.

sources.title: Motor-car principles; the gasoline automobile
sources.licenceSeen: Project Gutenberg ebook page, Copyright line reads 'Public domain in the USA.'
sources.needIt: Shows what is under the hood of a car: ignition, cooling, transmission, brakes.
sources.notes: Published 1907 per the Gutenberg page. No fuel injection, computers or emissions. Safety and repair steps are unsafe by today's standards (brakes, fuel, jacks).

sources.title: The gas-engine handbook. A manual of useful information for the designer and engineer
sources.licenceSeen: Archive page 'Possible copyright status: NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT', region US.
sources.needIt: Reference tables and designs for early engines; shows how power plants were sized.
sources.notes: Dense, for engineers. Use only for diagrams and history.

sources.title: Mechanics of the Household
sources.licenceSeen: Project Gutenberg ebook page, Copyright line reads 'Public domain in the USA.'
sources.needIt: Explains the machines in a house: pumps, heating, plumbing, simple electrical equipment.
sources.notes: Early 1900s; heating, plumbing and wiring advice is unsafe and out of code (lead pipe, gas lights). Flag each against current codes.

sources.title: Electric Bells and All About Them: A Practical Book for Practical Men
sources.licenceSeen: Project Gutenberg ebook page, Copyright line reads 'Public domain in the USA.'
sources.needIt: A hands-on introduction to circuits: a battery, wire, a bell and a push button.
sources.notes: Old batteries (zinc and acid) and mains advice; do not suggest connecting to house power. Safe version uses a 9 volt battery.

sources.title: Basic Electricity, NAVPERS 10086
sources.needIt: Explains circuits, magnets, motors and meters at a trainee's pace.
sources.notes: 1956 manual; large file (669 MB listed). Voltages, wire colors and materials are dated. Flag against the current electrical code.
